summary: Firestore rules use default-deny, verified-email admin authorization, strict ownership, field allowlists, type and size validation, immutable identity fields, backend-only Premium/IAP writes, and backend-only top-level daily limits. All 17 emulator tests pass. Two release integration gaps remain outside the rules: client-side account deletion now requires backend cleanup, and the Flutter admin gate still expects an admin custom claim.

findings.issue: Allowing users to delete users/{uid} would let a blocked account recreate the profile with isBlocked=false.
findings.recommendation: Client deletes are denied. Implement account deletion and Firestore cleanup with a trusted backend/Admin SDK.

findings.issue: The current client deletion flow queries reports and deletes traps. The requested admin-only report reads and admin-only trap writes correctly deny those operations.
findings.recommendation: Move account cleanup to a callable backend function and verify ownership server-side before deleting Auth, Firestore and Storage data.

findings.issue: Firestore and Storage rules recognize the exact verified email, but AdminAccessService in Flutter additionally requires the admin=true custom claim.
findings.recommendation: Until admin authorization is migrated fully to claims, set admin=true only for joa.rycyk@gmail.com so the existing admin UI can open.

findings.issue: Every field stored in traps and schools is public because Firestore rules cannot hide selected fields in a readable document.
findings.recommendation: Keep PII, moderation notes and internal metadata out of these public documents or move them to private subcollections.

remainingRisks: Enable and enforce Firebase App Check after monitoring valid TestFlight traffic.
Security Rules do not provide business-level rate limits for comments and reports; add backend quotas and abuse monitoring.
RevenueCat webhook processing must verify webhook authorization, be idempotent, and write Premium fields with Admin SDK.
Protect backend service accounts and Firestore IAM because Admin SDK bypasses Security Rules.
Deploy the committed rules to the correct Firebase project before release.
